title: Rollout telemetry playbook — signal minimalism & trace anchoring
content:
Purpose:
This playbook prescribes a compact, cost-aware telemetry surface for feature rollouts (canary, A/B, and progressive releases) in the inference stack. It prioritizes high-signal, low-cardinality metrics + trace anchors so engineers can evaluate rollout health quickly without exploding query costs or dashboard sprawl.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to model routing, cache warming, quantization toggles, and new batching strategies.
- Intended for short-lived rollout phases (hours → weeks) and post-rollout retros.
- Assumes common infra: per-request routing id, tenant id, region, model id, and route name are already available in logs/traces.
- Emphasize short retention for rollout-only dashboards (7–30 days) to reduce storage/query costs.

Guiding principles (decision heuristics):
1) Minimalism: start with 6–9 signals. If you need more, suspect design or instrumentation gaps.
2) Cardinality cap: avoid per-customer or per-input-cardinality in primary SLOs. Use sampling+replay for deep dives.
3) Correlation first: ensure a single, stable correlation key (rollout.trace_id or rollout_session_id) is attached to requests in rollout windows.
4) Cost-awareness: estimate expected query cost before adding any metric to the rollout dashboard. Default cost budget: 100 query-units/day for a canary.
5) Fast feedback: produce a short summary panel that answers "Is the rollout safe to expand?" within 3 clicks.

Signal matrix (recommended primary signals):
- rollout.requests.count — total requests hitting rollout cohort (sum, 1m rollup)
- rollout.request_latency.p50/p95 — end-to-end latency for requests in cohort (ms)
- rollout.kv_cache_hit_rate — percent of requests where KV cache avoided re-computation (ratio, 1m)
- rollout.token_cost.per_request — average tokens billed per request (avg over 5m)
- rollout.error_rate — percentage of requests returning non-200 or model-timeout (sum errors / sum requests)
- rollout.hallucination_proxy.rate — model quality signal (e.g. rerank-disagreement, sanity-check fails)
- rollout.fallback_rate — percent of requests that fell back to safe model variant
- rollout.queue_depth — scheduler queue depth for rollout pool (gauge)
- rollout.sampled_traces.count — number of traces captured for correlation (helps debugging)

Why these signals?
- Together they cover correctness (error/fallback/hallucination proxy), performance (latency, queue depth), and economics (token cost, kv cache).
- Each metric is intentionally aggregated first; drilling uses sampled traces or a low-cardinality log dump.

Metric naming and tagging conventions (short):
- Prefix with rollout. Use snake_case.
- Required tags: rollout_id, env (prod/staging), region, model_id, cohort (canary|control|baseline).
- Forbidden tags on primary SLOs: customer_id, request_hash. Put these on sampled logs only.

Trace anchoring & sampling strategy:
1) Rollout anchor: set trace tag rollout.session_id (a short UUID). Attach this at ingress and propagate to downstream services.
2) Span-level anchors: add span attribute rollout.phase (canary|expansion|rollback) and rollout.checkpoint for important decision points (cache-warm, model-switch).
3) Sampling policy:
   - Baseline sampling: 0.5% of all requests for control cohort.
   - Canary sampling: 5% of canary requests (adjust if canary traffic < 100 qps to ensure at least ~1 trace/s).
   - On-error increase: any error burst (error_rate > 1% absolute increase from baseline) temporarily boosts sampling to 50% for 10m.
4) Trace size cap: limit spans or truncate long user prompt content in traces to avoid PII and cost. Keep only input hash + length + sanitized first 500 chars.

Dashboard layout (compact rollout view):
Top row (health summary, 1 panel):
- One-line verdict: green/yellow/red derived from simple rule (error_rate, latency p95, fallback_rate). Shows raw values and % change vs baseline.
Row 2 (performance + economics, 3 small panels):
- latency p50/p95 trend (split canary/control)
- token_cost per_request (trend + numeric delta)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (trend)
Row 3 (correctness, 3 panels):
- error_rate (trend + top 3 error types)
- hallucination_proxy rate (trend + sample examples link)
- fallback_rate (trend)
Row 4 (operational context):
- queue_depth + scheduler utilization
- sampled_traces.count and button/link to trace explorer filtered by rollout.session_id
- cohort traffic split (percentages + absolute count)
Notes panel (bottom): short runbook and quick links (playbook checklist entries).

Dashboard surgery checklist (before you add a new metric or panel):
- Q1: Does this panel answer the rollout-safety question? If not, mark as investigatory and keep off the top row.
- Q2: Can we compute this from existing metrics + tags instead of adding new ETS points? Prefer derived metrics in dashboard queries.
- Q3: Cardinality check — estimated unique tag combinations/day < 1000? If >1000, move to sampled logs or reduce tag set.
- Q4: Query-cost estimate — run a dry-run of the query in dev for 24h; if cost > 20 query-units/day drop or lower resolution.
- Q5: Retention policy assigned (7/30/90 days) and owner added.

Alert guidance (temporary canary alerts):
- Use short-lived alerts scoped to rollout_id. Don't add to long-term SLOs.
- Example rules (fire when sustained for 3m unless otherwise stated):
  - error_rate > baseline + 1.5% absolute and error_rate > 0.75%
  - rollback trigger: fallback_rate > 5% OR hallucination_proxy.rate > baseline * 2
  - latency p95 > baseline p95 * 1.4 AND absolute p95 > 1200ms
- Alert destinations: oncall + rollout-owner + channel #rollouts-alerts. Attach context: rollout_id, snapshot of top metrics.

Debugging / investigation quick recipes:
1) High error rate but normal latency: check model variant mismatch and model warming logs. Pull recent traces filtered by rollout.session_id and error tag.
2) Latency spike with high queue_depth: inspect scheduler metrics, inspect batch sizes and draining patterns. Consider temporary scale-up of dedicated pool.
3) Increased token_cost with stable request volume: check prompt-length distribution and quantization toggles. Use token-length histogram.
4) Hallucination proxy increase: fetch 20 sampled inputs + model outputs, run reranker offline, and compare embeddings drift.

Instrumentation patterns (practical snippets — pseudocode):
- At ingress: 
  set rollout.session_id = env.rollout_manager.allocate_session()
  metric.increment('rollout.requests.count', tags={rollout_id, env, model_id, cohort})
  span.set_tag('rollout.session_id', rollout.session_id)

- When fallback occurs:
  metric.increment('rollout.fallback.count', tags={...})
  log.info('fallback', {rollout_id, reason, model_from, model_to, rollout.session_id})

- KV cache hit capture (emit both hit and total to compute ratio):
  metric.increment('rollout.kv_cache.hit', tags={...}) if hit
  metric.increment('rollout.kv_cache.total', tags={...})

Post-rollout retro checklist:
- Save snapshot of canary dashboard (CSV of top metrics) and attach to rollout ticket.
- Evaluate false positives in hallucination proxy; tune proxy threshold.
- Check metric and panel churn caused by rollout; decide which signals to promote to product dashboards.
- Run a cost delta analysis: additional query/storage cost for rollout duration.

Appendix: cost heuristics & sampling math (short)
- Query-unit estimate: approximate 1 complex timeseries query over 30d = 1 unit (example heuristic varies by backend). Use internal cost tool to convert.
- Sampling uplift math: if canary qps = 2 and we want ~1 trace/s, sampling_rate = min(1, desired_traces_per_s / (qps / avg_requests_per_s_per_instance)). For low-traffic canaries, prefer deterministic trace-on-every-nth-request.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define canonical rollout.session_id generator and lifecycle semantics (who creates/terminates).
- Integrate cohort labeling into ingress load-balancer for consistent telemetry tagging.
- Build a small UI in Console to pick a rollout and auto-create the compact dashboard from a template.
